statement: The supplied sources do not contain a derivation of the Extended Kalman Filter (they state the filter definitions and recursion equations without deriving them). By definition, the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is the nonlinear version of the Kalman filter which linearizes about an estimate of the current mean and covariance. For a continuous-time system model with discrete-time measurements given by \dot{\mathbf{x}}(t) = f(\mathbf{x}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)) + \mathbf{w}(t) with \mathbf{w}(t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{Q}(t)) and \mathbf{z}_k = h(\mathbf{x}_k) + \mathbf{v}_k with \mathbf{v}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{R}_k) where \mathbf{x}_k = \mathbf{x}(t_k), the first-order EKF is defined by the following equations: (1) Initialization: \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0|0} = E[\mathbf{x}(t_0)], \mathbf{P}_{0|0} = E[(\mathbf{x}(t_0) - \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_0))(\mathbf{x}(t_0) - \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_0))^T]; (2) Prediction: solve \dot{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}(t) = f(\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)) and \dot{\mathbf{P}}(t) = \mathbf{F}(t)\mathbf{P}(t) + \mathbf{P}(t)\mathbf{F}(t)^T + \mathbf{Q}(t) with \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_{k-1}) = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1|k-1}, \mathbf{P}(t_{k-1}) = \mathbf{P}_{k-1|k-1} \Rightarrow \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_k), \mathbf{P}_{k|k-1} = \mathbf{P}(t_k), where \mathbf{F}(t) = \left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial \mathbf{x}}\right|_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)}; (3) Update: \mathbf{K}_k = \mathbf{P}_{k|k-1}\mathbf{H}_k^T(\mathbf{H}_k\mathbf{P}_{k|k-1}\mathbf{H}_k^T + \mathbf{R}_k)^{-1}, \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1} + \mathbf{K}_k(\mathbf{z}_k - h(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1})), \mathbf{P}_{k|k} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_k\mathbf{H}_k)\mathbf{P}_{k|k-1}, where \mathbf{H}_k = \left.\frac{\partial h}{\partial \mathbf{x}}\right|_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1}}.

symbols.meaning: discrete state vector at time t_k, equal to \mathbf{x}(t_k)
discrete measurement vector at step k
process noise vector with covariance Q(t)
measurement noise vector with covariance R_k
predicted (a priori) state estimate at step k
updated (a posteriori) state estimate at step k
predicted (a priori) error covariance matrix at step k
updated (a posteriori) error covariance matrix at step k

properties.why: In the continuous-time extended Kalman filter, the prediction and update steps are coupled rather than separated into distinct stages
The update equations for continuous-time models with discrete-time measurements are identical to those of the discrete-time extended Kalman filter

properties.property: Extendability to higher orders via Taylor series
properties.why: Higher order EKFs (such as second and third order) are obtained by retaining more terms of the Taylor series expansions beyond the first-order Jacobians

The assumption of additive process and measurement noise is not necessary, allowing generalization to systems of the form \mathbf{x}_k = f(\mathbf{x}_{k-1}, \mathbf{u}_{k-1}, \mathbf{w}_{k-1}) and \mathbf{z}_k = h(\mathbf{x}_k, \mathbf{v}_k)

assumptions.assumption: Process noise w(t) and measurement noise v_k are zero-mean Gaussian distributed with covariances Q(t) and R_k
assumptions.breaks_when: The noise processes follow non-Gaussian distributions, multimodal distributions, or have nonzero unmodeled biases

assumptions.assumption: System dynamics f and measurement function h are sufficiently smooth and differentiable to permit first-order Taylor series linearization
assumptions.breaks_when: The dynamics or measurement models have severe non-differentiabilities, step discontinuities, or extreme local curvature

assumptions.assumption: The physical system has well-defined transition and measurement models
assumptions.breaks_when: The mathematical formulation of f or h is unknown or suffers from severe model structural errors

failure_modes.signature: State estimate diverges significantly from the ground truth while predicted error covariance remains unrealistically small
failure_modes.cause: First-order Taylor series truncation error becomes dominant when system nonlinearities are severe or the estimation error is large

failure_modes.mode: Lack of performance gain for higher-order EKFs under large measurement noise
failure_modes.signature: Second- or third-order filter implementations yield no improvement over the first-order EKF despite higher computational cost
failure_modes.cause: Higher order EKFs tend to only provide performance benefits when the measurement noise is small

failure_modes.mode: Numerical ill-conditioning of the innovation covariance matrix
failure_modes.signature: Matrix inversion (\mathbf{H}_k \mathbf{P}_{k|k-1} \mathbf{H}_k^T + \mathbf{R}_k)^{-1} fails or produces indefinite updated covariance \mathbf{P}_{k|k}
failure_modes.cause: Singular or near-singular measurement covariance \mathbf{R}_k, or loss of positive-definiteness due to floating-point rounding in the update subtraction
